items.q: The pair of CT/MR angiogram images drawn to the right of the renal doppler picture carries which caption?
items.exp: The two panels (A and B, each with a white arrow) are captioned 'unilateral renal artery stenosis'; the separate caption 'Bilateral renal artery stenosis' belongs to the aortogram lower on the page. (Book p751)

items.q: An 8 cm left kidney is normal and the right, stenosed kidney measures 6.5 cm; blood pressure is controlled on ramipril. Per the treatment block, angioplasty is:
opts: Not offered, because PTRA is listed only if kidney size is greater than 8 cm
Offered at once, since the stenosis is unilateral
Offered only after a trial of diuretics
Not offered, because PTRA is reserved for bilateral disease
items.exp: The unilateral treatment block lists ACE inhibitors/ARBs (DOC) and PTRA '- Only if kidney size > 8 cm'; the 6.5 cm kidney fails that condition. (Book p751)

items.q: Match each drug class with where the page calls it the drug of choice — 1) ACE inhibitors/ARBs 2) Diuretics … A) Blood pressure in bilateral RAS B) Unilateral RAS C) Neither, both are contraindicated in RAS
items.exp: ACE inhibitors/ARBs are DOC in unilateral RAS but contraindicated in bilateral RAS (they ↓GFR), where diuretics take over as the DOC for blood pressure. (Book p751)
